question: Recently, the agricultural world has been facing serious problems and has begun mobilising on a large scale. Farmers are coming under pressure due to high operating costs, high prices, the low retail price of products and uncertainty regarding the future. Extreme, fluctuating weather conditions have an adverse effect on agricultural production, increasing the risk of losses and affecting sustainability.

The CAP 2023-27 supports new production models that are based on boosting competitiveness and are designed to deal with the challenges of climate change, for example competitiveness-boosting investment plans, which include a variety of initiatives for the use of sophisticated new technologies, such as precision farming, remote-controlled processes, automation and digitalisation of agricultural holdings/farms.

Crop management is based on dynamic processes and requires careful and precise planning on a daily basis, as well as the management of farming activities on a strategic, tactical and operational level.

The adoption of a step-by-step, structured decision-making process can help farmers/ agronomists/crop managers to take better informed and more considered decisions, organising relevant information and coming up with alternative solutions. In view of this: 1.
How does the Commission intend to help with the above through the new CAP, so that everyone benefits from smart farming?
What steps does it plan to take to tackle existing problems and support farmers in promoting sustainable practices in agriculture?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.3.2024) Support for enhancing the competitiveness and sustainability of farm operations by means of digital and data-enabled technologies is an integral part of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2023-2027[1] which focuses strongly on knowledge, innovation and digitalisation.

Under their CAP Strategic Plans, Member States have elaborated digitalisation strategies outlining the intended use of CAP interventions such as investment support, eco-schemes and agro-environment-climate commitments, training and farm advice to help farmers adopt smart farming solutions, according to the national needs.

Precision farming technologies such as sensors, drones and satellite imagery can help optimise the use of inputs by supporting the collection and analysis of real-time data such as soil moisture, nutrient levels, weather patterns and crop health.

Data can be used to inform crop management strategies including irrigation and fertilisation practices, leading to higher yields, and reduced costs and impact on the environment. The development of the Common European Agricultural Dataspace[2] will allow farmers to further generate value from their data.

Through CAP support, the promotion of integrated strategies combining farming practices with digital technologies, could bring enhanced benefits. The Commission works closely with the Member States to ensure the CAP Strategic Plans deliver on their digital strategies for the benefits of all farmers.

Opportunities offered by improved use of technological innovation (including digital solutions) is among the key challenges that will be addressed within the strategic dialogue on the future of agriculture, launched by the Commission on 25 January 2024[3].
